title: Disentangling QAOA: From Weakly Entangled Circuits to a Classical QUBO Solver
authors: Boris I. Bantysh, Andrey Yu. Chernyavskiy, Denis A. Kulikov, Maksim A. Gavreev, Evgeniy O. Kiktenko
abstract: The role of entanglement in quantum optimization remains actively debated. To address this question, we focus on the fixed-parameter expanding-depth regime of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), where a compact two-parameter schedule is trained once on small instances and then applied as the problem size and circuit depth increase. To probe this regime beyond full state-vector simulation, we perform approximate matrix product state simulations for up to 50 qubits and 100 layers and quantify entanglement by the bond dimension. We observe an entangle--disentangle profile, with the peak bond dimension decreasing with depth and eventually saturating. This observation motivates an extreme approximation: projecting the state onto the product-state manifold (bond dimension one) after every two-qubit interaction. Based on this approximation, we introduce BOND-1, a quantum-inspired classical solver. Despite the drastic simplification, BOND-1 achieves cut ratios above 0.95 relative to the best known values on standard GSet MaxCut benchmarks with up to 20000 variables, and in some cases it matches those values. It achieves these results without per-instance optimization and has linear memory cost, while per-instance tuning can provide further improvement. These results show that, in this regime, a substantial fraction of the optimization power of QAOA survives even in the complete absence of entanglement. Our conclusions, however, are specific to this setting and do not imply that entanglement is unnecessary for quantum optimization in general.
summary: This work examines how much of QAOA's optimization power remains when entanglement is artificially suppressed by projecting the quantum state onto a product basis. By developing the classical solver BOND-1, the authors show that even in the absence of entanglement, the algorithm maintains high performance on complex optimization problems, provided the circuit depth is large enough.
main_problem: The paper investigates the role of entanglement in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) by analyzing its dynamics in the fixed-parameter expanding-depth regime.
main_result: A classical solver, BOND-1, derived by projecting the quantum state onto the product-state manifold (zero entanglement), achieves high cut ratios (>0.95) on large MaxCut benchmarks, suggesting optimization power survives without entanglement in this regime.
method: The authors use approximate Matrix Product State (MPS) simulations to track entanglement dynamics and then introduce a quantum-inspired classical solver (BOND-1) based on projecting the state evolution onto the product-state manifold.
model_or_system: The model is QAOA applied to QUBO optimization problems, encoded via an Ising Hamiltonian. The simulation tracks the state evolution $| eta, \gammaangle$ using MPS formalism.
key_observables: Bond dimension ($\chi$), entanglement entropy, and the resulting cut ratio on GSet MaxCut benchmarks.
important_parameters: Fixed-parameter schedule parameters $(v, u)$, circuit depth ($p$), and problem size ($n$).
main_assumptions: The results are specific to the fixed-parameter expanding-depth regime, and the core approximation is projecting the state onto the product-state manifold ($\chi=1$) after every two-qubit interaction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QAOA layer structure, the entanglement dynamics showing an 'entangle–disentangle' profile, and the maximum bond dimension ($\chi_{	ext{max}}$) as a function of depth, which saturates.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the QAOA framework and the need for simulation methods (MPS). It then analyzes the entanglement profile, leading to the proposal of the extreme approximation (BOND-1). Finally, it demonstrates BOND-1's performance on large-scale benchmarks.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, computationally tractable method (BOND-1) to estimate QAOA performance by drastically simplifying the quantum state, which is highly relevant for near-term quantum hardware limitations.

Contour levels indicate different normalized approximation levels, and the black star marks the selected point (u∗, v∗) = (3.384, −0.071).
